It affects Axios version 1.15.2 specifically, representing an incomplete fix for a prior prototype pollution issue (GHSA-q8qp-cvcw-x6jj). The vulnerability was published on May 29, 2026, and patched in version 1.16.0. It carries a CVSS v3.1 base score of 3.7 (Low) per the NVD/GitHub Advisory Database, though the advisory author assessed it as Medium (5.6) (GitHub Advisory, Red Hat Bugzilla). Technical details The root cause is an incomplete null-prototype fix in Axios 1.15.2: while the top-level config object was hardened with Object.create(null), nested objects produced by utils.merge() (e.g., config.proxy) are still created as plain {} literals that inherit from Object.prototype (CWE-1321). The setProxy() function in lib/adapters/http.js (lines 209–223) reads proxy.username, proxy.password, and proxy.auth without hasOwnProperty checks, so if Object.prototype.username is polluted by a separate vulnerability in the dependency tree, the function constructs a Proxy-Authorization header using attacker-controlled credentials and injects it into every proxied HTTP request (CWE-113). Exploitation requires two preconditions: the application must explicitly configure config.proxy, and a separate prototype pollution gadget must exist elsewhere in the dependency tree to pollute Object.prototype.username or Object.prototype.auth (GitHub Advisory). Impact Successful exploitation allows an unauthenticated attacker to inject arbitrary Proxy-Authorization headers into all proxied HTTP requests made by the affected application, effectively spoofing the proxy identity. This can result in proxy log poisoning (attacker credentials recorded instead of legitimate user credentials), access control bypass if the proxy enforces authentication-based policies, and credential injection amplification if transparent proxies forward the header upstream. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact; browser-side impact is generally constrained by browser process limits and is not considered server process exhaustion (GitHub Advisory).
